answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by letting trust be lent, not minted. A newcomer earns visibility only when established peers endorse it with a slice of their own stake, like copper tokens pinned to a shared atlas of reputations. Each endorsement is weighted by the endorser's record, but it decays unless distinct, reputable peers renew it after real, verifiable work. A whisper network of fake copies therefore gains nothing by multiplying: copies share no stake, and each one still needs fresh, costly backing from different honest agents to remain trusted.
